body:
did you know: the girl in "august" almost had a name.

she's the third narrator of folklore's teenage love triangle -- the summer that "slipped away" -- and she is never once named in the lyrics. it was in the long pond sessions that taylor mused the character might be "augusta. or augustine." fans took that and made it canon.

taylor wrote and produced her with jack antonoff as the triangle's sympathetic wildcard: the girl who deserved kindness, not blame, for a romance that was never really hers. "august" entered the hot 100 at no. 23 in the album's opening week, and that outro -- the full-orchestra major-chord climax -- is the biggest purely musical moment on the record. rob sheffield later ranked it fifth in her entire catalog, "the album's most plainly beautiful ballad."

happy salt-air month. the girl who slipped away has a whole one named after her now.

longlivets.com
why: Timely folklore did-you-know riding the 'salt-air month' fan ritual peaking this week (see today's listening scan: Swifties are re-streaming 'august' and calling August 'salt air month'). Strong why-now hook while staying in warm song-craft lore. Every claim traces to the Vault folklore item 'august, and the girl Taylor says might be named Augusta. Or Augustine.' (sourced Wikipedia 'August (Taylor Swift song)'): the unnamed third narrator of the cardigan/august/betty love triangle, Taylor musing 'Augusta or Augustine' in the Long Pond Sessions, written+produced with Jack Antonoff, Hot 100 debut at No. 23 in the opening week, the full-orchestra major-chord outro, and Rob Sheffield's 2021 Rolling Stone catalog ranking (5th, 'the album's most plainly beautiful ballad'). 'salt air' is a real lyric from the song. Song-craft lore only -- outside every #36/Clownbot blocklist topic. Media: /eras/folklore.png (committed, deployed era tile). Scheduled 08-09 23:00 (~7pm ET) to hold the evening cadence in the next open slot after the queued reputation (08-07) and fifteen (08-08) items.
failureReason:
Stuck 2 days past scheduledAt and retired here by hand on 2026-08-11 rather than shipped late.

WHY IT NEVER POSTED: its media is /eras/folklore.png, generic era-cover art that was already used by 2026-08-01-invisible-string-thread-ig.json (posted 2026-08-04). The repetition guard added on 2026-08-06 therefore skipped it on every 30-minute run WITHOUT spending an attempt — correct behaviour, since this is an authoring gap and not a transient failure, but it also meant the item could never reach 3 attempts and so could never land here on its own. Only ~4 more Instagram posts would have aged folklore.png out of the 10-post lookback, i.e. mid-August at the current cadence.

WHY NOT JUST SHIP IT LATE: the copy is August-wide ("happy salt-air month"), not locked to the 9th, so lateness alone would not disqualify it. Two other things do. Its X twin (2026-08-09-august-augustine-x.json) published on schedule with the same sourced facts, so the campaign has already run on the other platform. And its why-now hook was a specific week's listening scan; a week later that hook is gone. Shipping it in mid-August on a repeated era tile would be worse than not shipping it.

WHAT TO DO WITH IT: the writing is fine and fully sourced. Requeue it with a REAL dedicated photo rather than an era tile — PR #1903 is seeding apps/web/public/social/library/**, which makes that cheap — and give it a fresh scheduledAt. Do not requeue it as-is.

CLASS FIX (same PR): a skip that spends no attempt can no longer hide. run-report.mjs escalates any skipped/waiting item past 24h overdue to an ::error:: annotation and a non-zero exit, so the next item like this reddens the run instead of logging into a green one for two days.
